# SeaRM Trademark Policy

"SeaRM", the SeaRM logo, and searm.com are trademarks of SeaRM.com, PBC ("SeaRM"), whether registered or unregistered. The source code of SeaRM is open source under the licenses described in [LICENSE](../LICENSE); those licenses do not grant any rights to use our trademarks.

The goal of this policy is simple: anyone should be able to say truthfully that they use, build on, or contribute to SeaRM, and nobody should suggest an affiliation with or endorsement by SeaRM that does not exist, or confuse users about what comes from us.

## You can, without asking

- Use and self-host SeaRM, modified or not, for yourself or your organization, and say that you do.
- Make truthful statements such as "built on SeaRM", "compatible with SeaRM", "powered by SeaRM", or "we host SeaRM for our clients".
- Name an application or integration "X for SeaRM" or "SeaRM integration for X", as long as your own brand is the dominant element and you do not use our logo as your own.
- Use the name "SeaRM" to refer to the project in articles, talks, tutorials, courses, and comparisons.
- Link to searm.com and use unmodified screenshots of the product.

## You need our written permission to

- Use "SeaRM" or a confusingly similar name in the name of your company, product, service, domain name, social media account, or app store listing (for example "SearmCloud" or "searm-hosting.com").
- Market a hosted, managed, or modified version of SeaRM in a way that suggests it is an official SeaRM offering, or is endorsed by or affiliated with SeaRM.
- Use the SeaRM logo as, or as part of, your own logo or branding.
- Sell merchandise bearing the SeaRM name or logo.

## Forks

You may maintain and distribute forks of the source code under the terms of the applicable licenses. If you distribute or operate a fork publicly, give it its own name and branding. You may state truthfully that it is "a fork of SeaRM", but do not use the SeaRM name or logo in a way that suggests your fork is the original project.

## Questions

If you are unsure whether your use is allowed, or want to request permission, open an issue on GitHub or contact us through searm.com.
